jobs.title: Cloud Architecture & Engineering, Director
jobs.description:
At PwC, our people in data and analytics engineering focus on leveraging advanced technologies and techniques to design and develop robust data solutions for clients. They play a crucial role in transforming raw data into actionable insights, enabling informed decision-making and driving business growth. Those in machine learning ops engineering at PwC will focus on developing and implementing operational processes and infrastructure to support machine learning models and algorithms. Your work will involve enabling the smooth deployment and maintenance of machine learning systems within an organisation.

The Opportunity

As a Cloud Architecture & Engineering, Director, unlock your potential and embrace the chance to drive meaningful outcomes that’ll elevate your career. Your role will include, but isn’t limited to:

You will play a pivotal leadership role at the intersection of cloud strategy, architecture, engineering, and client engagement.  
This role combines deep technical cloud expertise with strategic leadership, practice development, and team coaching.  
You will shape and scale cloud capabilities, guide clients through complex transformation journeys, and help drive PwC’s cloud first vision. 
You will be responsible for designing and governing enterprise grade cloud architectures while also driving advisory engagements, leading teams, strengthening client relationships, and contributing to the innovation pipeline for cloud-based solutions and assets. 
This role requires a seasoned cloud leader who can operate fluently across business strategy, modern cloud architectures, and hands-on technical depth—while mentoring teams and influencing both internal and client executives.
Lead the design, governance, and implementation of end-to-end cloud architectures aligned to business goals and industry best practices. 
Architect scalable, secure, and cost optimized cloud solutions across AWS, Azure, and GCP. 
Develop cloud foundation blueprints, reference architectures, and reusable patterns. 
Oversee the design and optimization of Kubernetes platforms (EKS, AKS, GKE) and containerized environments. 
Guide the development and automation of cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, AWS CDK, ARM, etc.). 
Provide technical guidance on compute, storage, networking, security, identity, data services, and DevOps tooling. 
Serve as a trusted advisor to executive-level stakeholders, helping them define and execute cloud strategies and operating models. 
Assess existing environments, develop modernization roadmaps, and oversee cloud migration programs. 
Lead proposal creation, solutioning activities, statements of work, and client presentations. 
Communicate complex technical concepts to nontechnical audiences clearly and effectively. 
Identify and prioritize client use cases and translate business requirements into architectural approaches and execution plans. 
Build, lead, and mentor teams of cloud architects, engineers, and technical specialists. 
Foster a culture of continuous learning, experimentation, and cloud innovation. 
Recruit and grow diverse technical talent, ensuring strong career development and retention. 
Collaborate with practice leadership to define strategic direction, emerging offerings, and go-to-market assets. 
Lead initiatives that strengthen practice foundations: capability models, delivery frameworks, accelerators, patterns, and reusable assets. 
Lead technical innovation cycles to evaluate, test, and showcase new cloud technologies, tools, and architectures. 
Drive and participate in hands-on cloud prototyping, labbing, and solution validation. 
Develop technical demos, asset-driven solutions, and market-aligned accelerators. 
Present at internal and external events, contributing to PwC’s thought leadership presence. 
Maintain active engagement with cloud provider alliances and product engineering teams to share early insights and influence product evolution. 

What You'll Bring

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here's what we look for:

Extensive experience in cloud architecture and engineering across AWS (primary), Azure, and/or GCP. 
Deep knowledge of Kubernetes, containers, microservices, serverless architectures, and modern DevOps practices. 
Hands-on experience with IaC tools (Terraform strongly preferred), CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Argo, etc.), and automated deployment patterns. 
Strong understanding of cloud security, IAM, network segmentation, encryption, monitoring, cost optimization, and governance frameworks. 
Experience supporting modernization programs such as application migration, refactoring, API strategies, and technical debt remediation. 
AI-assisted development and prior experience deploying agentic workloads and MLOps pipelines is an asset.
Demonstrated experience leading cloud-focused teams and initiatives in a complex, multistakeholder environment. 
Strong executive communication skills suitable for client-facing consulting environments. 
Ability to bridge business and technical perspectives and articulate value propositions, architecture decisions, and tradeoffs. 
Strategic mindset with a bias toward execution, innovation, and measurable impact. 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience). 
Significant cloud architecture and engineering leadership experience. 
Preferred:  AWS Solutions Architect (Professional); Azure or GCP Architect certifications; Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or CKAD; Terraform Associate Certification.
As a requirement, a Security Clearance is mandatory for all staff who’ll be engaged on these assignments. Prior to applying, please review the Government of Canada website to ensure you meet the eligibility requirements to obtain this clearance. This’ll become a condition of your employment with PwC should you receive an offer from us.
This role does not require professional engineering licensure and is not classified as a formal engineering position under provincial regulatory definitions. While individuals with a P.Eng designation are welcome to apply, the responsibilities of this role do not involve the practice of professional engineering as defined by applicable legislation.

jobs.title: SVP, IT Operations
jobs.description:
Summary

JOB DESCRIPTION

The Senior Vice President, IT Operations is accountable for the stability, performance, resilience, secure operation and continuous improvement of the technology environment that supports BGIS operations and the business-critical solutions we deliver to our clients. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, this executive leads four operational domains: Application Support, Infrastructure (including Service Desk and End User Support), Financial Application Support, and the Legacy Software Development Platform (operational enhancements). The individual sets the operational strategy and service model for these domains, directs a team of directors, managers and technical professionals across onshore and offshore teams, and partners with business unit leaders, client-facing teams and vendors to ensure that services meet or exceed contractual SLAs and client expectations. The individual drives a culture of operational excellence and continuous improvement, using automation, standardization, data-driven KPI management and modern IT service management practices to increase reliability, reduce cost, and improve the client and end-user experience. The role is a member of the IT leadership team and reports regularly to senior and executive management on operational performance, risk and investment priorities.

Key Duties & Responsibilities

Leadership

Directs the IT Operations organization through a team of directors and managers, spanning onshore, offshore and third-party resources across all four domains.

Demonstrates strong, competent leadership for team members to guide them in reaching their full potential and meeting their objectives, which supports achievement of our corporate goals. Specifically, these responsibilities include but not limited to:

Full involvement with recruiting talent.
Provides mentoring, coaching and guidance to all team members.
Objectively recommends compensation adjustments.
Manages all aspects of performance.
Builds leadership bench strength and succession plans across all four IT Operations domains.
Develops the technical capabilities of the organization, including reskilling and upskilling staff for cloud, automation and AI-enabled operations.
Defines the workforce and sourcing strategy, determining the right balance of in-house, offshore and managed service resources.
Fosters an environment of teamwork, accountability, innovation and client service to meet business objectives.

IT Operations Strategy & Service Excellence

Defines and executes the multi-year IT Operations strategy and roadmap, aligned with BGIS business objectives, client commitments and the broader IT strategy.
Partners with the Chief Technology Officer and Architecture to shape the enterprise technology roadmap and standards, and leads the operational integration of acquired businesses and new technology platforms.
Holds overall accountability for the availability, performance and resiliency of business-critical solutions that support our clients, ensuring contractual SLAs and KPIs are consistently met or exceeded.
Establishes a unified operating model, service catalogue and support structure (L1-L3) across Application Support, Infrastructure, Financial Application Support and the Legacy Software Development Platform.
Establishes demand intake, prioritization and resource capacity planning across all four domains, balancing day-to-day operations, operational projects, CISO-requested security work and client commitments, and ensures operational projects are delivered on time, on budget and with minimal service disruption.
Establishes governance for ITSM processes, including incident, major incident, problem, change, release, configuration and request management, and ensures timely root-cause analysis and corrective action.
Ensures 24x7 operational coverage for business-critical services, including monitoring and event management, and on-call and after-hours support.
Serves as the executive escalation point for critical client-impacting incidents; directs response, client communication and post-incident reviews.
Builds relationships with senior business unit leaders and client-facing teams to understand business direction, anticipate operational needs and manage expectations.
Provides service performance insights to account and client-facing teams to inform client governance discussions and shape the support model, and ensures IT services comply with client contractual, audit and data protection requirements.
Establishes and enforces IT Operations policies, standards and procedures, and ensures adherence to enterprise IT standards (i.e. Security, IT Governance, Service Management, Architecture).
Manages operational risks through mitigation strategies, and plans or implements contingencies where necessary.
Provides regular reporting to senior and executive management on SLA and KPI performance, operational risk, capacity and investment priorities.

Application Support

Directs the support, maintenance and operational health of the enterprise and client-facing application portfolio, including integrations, middleware and SaaS platforms.
Ensures applications that support client service delivery are monitored, supported and maintained to meet defined service levels and business continuity requirements.
Partners with Business Technology, product and development teams to ensure smooth transition of new solutions into production support, including defining operational acceptance criteria early in the delivery lifecycle.
Sets the strategy for application lifecycle management, including patching, upgrades, license compliance, and the rationalization and decommissioning of redundant applications.
Oversees database administration and data operations, including performance, backup and restore, and data retention, in line with BGIS and client requirements.

Infrastructure & End User Support

Leads the strategy, engineering and operation of the infrastructure environment, including data centre and cloud platforms, servers, storage, networks and telephony.
Directs the Service Desk and End User Support functions, including end-user computing, mobile devices, collaboration tools and field support, ensuring a consistent, high-quality experience for employees and client-facing staff.
Ensures infrastructure capacity, performance and resiliency meet current and future business and client requirements.
Owns IT disaster recovery and partners with the Business Continuity Planning (BCP) team to ensure IT systems meet BCP objectives; ensures DR plans are documented and tested regularly.
Establishes IT asset and configuration management practices, including hardware and software asset lifecycle and an accurate configuration management database (CMDB).
Advances infrastructure modernization, including cloud adoption, observability, AIOps and infrastructure automation.

Financial Application Support

Directs the operation, support and operational enhancement of the financial application landscape (e.g. ERP, general ledger, accounts payable/receivable, billing, procurement and related integrations).
Partners with Finance leadership to ensure financial systems reliably support month-end, quarter-end and year-end close, client billing and financial reporting cycles.
Ensures appropriate IT general controls, segregation of duties and audit readiness in support of internal controls over financial reporting and internal and external audit requirements.
Establishes governance with Finance stakeholders for prioritizing financial system changes, enhancements and upgrades.

Legacy Software Development Platform (Operational Enhancements)

Leads the team responsible for sustaining and enhancing legacy and custom-developed software platforms that continue to support business-critical operations and client solutions.
Establishes the intake and prioritization framework for operational enhancements, defect fixes and minor changes, balancing business value, risk and capacity.
Ensures sound software change management practices, including source control, release and deployment management, testing, quality assurance and release sign-off.
Reduces technical debt and operational risk of legacy platforms, and partners with Architecture and Business Technology to define modernization, migration or retirement roadmaps.

Security & Compliance Support

Partners with the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), delivering the technology work required for security projects and programs as they are raised.
Ensures operational security practices are consistently executed across IT Operations in accordance with CISO-defined policies, including access management, vulnerability and patch management, backup and secure configuration.
Supports the CISO during security incidents by providing technical response, recovery and remediation resources.
Supports compliance, certification and client audit activities by providing operational evidence and remediating identified gaps.

Continuous Improvement

Champions a culture of continuous improvement, using operational data, trend analysis and client feedback to identify and remove recurring issues and inefficiencies.
Drives automation, self-service, standardization and AI-enabled tooling to improve service quality, speed of resolution and cost-effectiveness.
Ensures knowledge management, runbooks and documentation practices are maintained across all IT Operations domains to enable shift-left resolution, self-service and reduced reliance on key individuals.
Establishes meaningful, business-focused KPIs and dashboards for each domain and uses them to set improvement targets and measure progress.
Introduces and matures industry best practices (e.g. ITIL, Lean, SRE and DevOps principles) across IT Operations.
Applies BGIS AI policies and establishes operating guidelines for the responsible use of AI and automation within IT Operations.
Evaluates emerging technologies and recommends investments that improve reliability, reduce risk and deliver value to our clients.

Financial & Vendor Management

Develops and manages the IT Operations operating and capital budgets; identifies opportunities for cost optimization while protecting service quality.
Applies cloud financial management (FinOps) practices to monitor, allocate and optimize cloud consumption costs.
Manages strategic vendor, managed service provider and outsourcing relationships, including contract negotiation, performance management and SLA governance.
Ensures managed service providers, offshore and third-party resources meet BGIS and client security, privacy and contractual obligations, in partnership with the CISO and Procurement.
Supports proposal and client transition teams by defining operational support models and service commitments, and ensures client data, access and integrations are transitioned or decommissioned in line with contractual obligations when client contracts end.
Other duties as assigned.

Knowledge & Skills

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business or equivalent; Master's Degree or MBA is an asset.
Minimum 15 years of progressive IT experience, including at least 8 years in senior leadership roles within IT Operations, infrastructure and application support.
Proven experience leading large, multi-disciplinary teams through multiple layers of management, including onshore, offshore and third-party resources.
Demonstrated track record of supporting business-critical, client-facing solutions in a service delivery or outsourced services environment with contractual SLAs.
Strong working knowledge of enterprise infrastructure (cloud, data centre, network, end-user computing), service desk operations, application support, and IT service management (ITIL) practices.
Experience supporting financial/ERP systems and IT general controls in an audited environment.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
jobs.description:
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer | Location: Toronto, Ontario [hybrid] | Full-time, permanent

About Us

Appficiency is a global technology and professional services firm that solves complex business challenges through the intelligent application of enterprise software, automation, and AI. We're a proud Oracle NetSuite Alliance Partner; Salesforce Crest Partner; Microsoft Gold Certified Partner, and much more: our evolution has taken us well beyond a single platform, making us a multi-technology advisory and implementation partner across ERP, CRM, cloud platforms, and AI-driven solutions. What sets us apart is a "technical-first" approach, teams who understand both business logic and deep system architecture paired with a genuine belief that our people are our greatest strength, and that's who we invest in first.

The Opportunity

As our first CFO, you will be the senior-most financial leader of the organization — owning financial strategy, acquisition strategy and the overall fiscal health of the business as we navigate our next phase of growth as a services-led technology firm, scaling through both organic growth and acquisitions. You'll work closely with the CEO and the executive team to drive sustainable revenue growth and profitability, improve financial performance and build a finance function that gives leadership timely, reliable information for decisions. Our day-to-day finance operations are sound; this role adds the senior leadership layer above them. It suits a seasoned finance executive who can do three things well: build the function (processes, reporting and budgeting), develop the team and lead acquisitions from screening through integration.

What You'll Do

Develop and execute financial strategies that align with the company's growth objectives, including a growth plan that separates organic growth from acquisition-driven growth and tracks both against actual results
Oversee all financial operations, including FP&A, accounting, treasury, budgeting, and risk management across our Toronto and Philippines teams
Lead the strategic financial planning process, including long-term projections and capital allocation decisions made with the CEO
Act as the CEO's senior deputy on financial and operational matters, able to represent the company and lead decisions in the CEO's absence
Build and deliver a monthly management reporting package (results, budget-to-actual analysis, key performance indicators and commentary) on a fixed calendar, so leadership receives the information it needs without having to request it
Lead the annual budget with department heads so each leader understands and owns their budget, and connect it to the unit economics of the business
Oversee company cash flow, investments, and capital structure optimization
Manage financial reporting and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, including tax, payroll and statutory filings in each country where we operate
Set revenue recognition, billing and project accounting policies for fixed-fee, time-and-materials and software resale contracts
Lead mergers and acquisitions from end to end: set acquisition criteria; screen opportunities sourced by our advisors; lead valuation, financial due diligence and deal structuring; and plan post-acquisition integration
Manage relationships with banks, lenders, auditors and external advisors; lead any future financing
Build and lead the finance and accounting team; coach and develop current team members into larger roles and add capability (such as FP&A) as the business grows
Analyze key professional services metrics (utilization, realization, project margin, backlog, collections) and software metrics (recurring revenue, renewals, churn) to drive profitability and growth decisions
Partner with the CEO and executive team on strategic decision-making and operational efficiency
Collaborate with the CTO and other executives to align financial and technology strategy
Partner with the leader of our internal transformation program so finance processes and reporting support company-wide operating improvements
Identify financial risks, maintain effective internal controls and develop mitigation strategies to protect company assets
Prepare the business for potential future milestones (e.g. significant acquisitions, major growth investments or a future transaction)

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field; Master's degree or MBA preferred
12-15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant time as a CFO or senior finance executive in a professional services or technology firm, ideally an IT consulting or systems integration business
CPA designation (or equivalent international accounting designation) required; CFA an asset
Executive experience with professional services and software business models and associated revenue recognition
Proven experience scaling a mid-market business toward $100M in revenue, including growth through acquisitions
A builder's track record: designing finance processes, management reporting and budgeting from the ground up, ideally as a company's first CFO
Strong track record driving financial strategy in high-growth, founder-led or owner-managed environments
Deep understanding of professional services economics (utilization, rates, project margin) and software metrics and their strategic implications
Excellent leadership skills, with experience building and scaling finance teams and mentoring early-career finance leaders
Outstanding communication skills, comfortable engaging the CEO, department heads, lenders and acquisition counterparties; able to explain financial results clearly to non-financial leaders
International finance experience (multi-country teams and foreign currency) is a plus
Hands-on experience with Oracle NetSuite (or a comparable cloud ERP) is a strong asset

What Will Set You Apart

A track record of successfully leading acquisitions of professional services or technology businesses, from screening through integration
Deep fluency in services and software unit economics and how they inform strategic decision-making
A reputation for clear, credible financial communication with owners, lenders and leadership teams
Experience preparing a company for significant milestones (acquisition, major scale-up)
A collaborative, tech-forward mindset — comfortable partnering with product and technology leaders
Experience coaching a high-potential finance manager into a senior leadership role
Comfort stepping into a finance framework established by an interim CFO or external advisors and making it your own

What Success Looks Like

The company's financial strategy directly enables and accelerates growth objectives
The CEO and leadership team view you as a trusted, credible voice on financial health and strategy
Leadership receives a monthly management reporting package on a fixed calendar, without having to request it
Department heads own their budgets and use them to run their areas
Acquisition opportunities are screened against clear criteria and the transactions you lead are executed and integrated smoothly
The finance team operates as a strategic partner to the business, not just a reporting function
The Finance team has grown into larger roles, with clear accountabilities and succession in place
Financial risk is proactively managed, and the company is well-positioned for its next growth milestone

jobs.description:
About Xanadu:

Xanadu’s mission is to build quantum computers that are useful and available to people everywhere.

At Xanadu, we are learners, innovators, researchers, collaborators and problem solvers. We are creating something that has never been built before. What we are doing is extremely hard, the classic moon shot. Few people in their life will be able to be a part of something like this, where if we are successful, the technologies we develop will solve some of the world’s most challenging problems, and literally change the world. And that is something to be excited about!

Your role and responsibilities:

The Director, Internal Controls and projects is responsible for supporting management in the design, implementation, execution, and continuous improvement of the Company's processes and internal control programs, including the Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance program. This role will partner with finance, operations, information technology, Internal Audit, External Audit, IT and business process owners to strengthen the control environment, support regulatory compliance, and drive process improvement initiatives.

The Director will lead internal controls activities on management’s behalf, assist with management's evaluation of internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR), deliver training to control owners and stakeholders, and participate in other finance projects as required such as financial and system transformations.

You will:
Internal Controls and SOX Compliance:

Support management in the implementation, maintenance, and enhancement of the Company's internal control and SOX compliance programs.
Coordinate related planning activities, risk assessments, process reviews, and control rationalization in collaboration with internal audit.
Assist management in evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal controls including for SOX compliance.
Partner with process owners to improve processes and related control documentation, and prepare and maintain control documentation.
Coordinate management testing activities and monitor the timely execution of key controls.
Track control deficiencies, remediation plans, and management action items to ensure timely resolution.
Support management's quarterly and annual control certification processes.
Evaluate control implications arising from changes in business processes, organizational structures, systems, and regulatory requirements.
Promote continuous improvement of internal controls through the identification and implementation of best practices, process improvements, and automation opportunities.

Audit Collaboration:

Collaborate closely with Internal Audit and External Audit to support SOX compliance, control assessments, and audit activities.
Coordinate with Internal Audit and External Audit on testing plans, documentation requirements, walkthroughs, and evidence requests.
Facilitate management responses to audit observations and assist in the development and execution of remediation plans.
Foster alignment among management, Internal Audit, and External Audit regarding key risks, control design, testing approaches, and remediation activities.
Support efforts to maximize audit efficiencies and reliance opportunities through high-quality documentation and control execution.

Training and Business Partnership:

Develop and deliver training programs related to SOX compliance, internal controls, governance, and risk management.
Provide guidance and support to control owners and business stakeholders regarding internal control responsibilities and expectations.
Promote a strong culture of accountability, compliance, and risk awareness throughout the organization.
Act as a trusted advisor to management on internal control, governance, and compliance matters.

Systems Implementations and Special Projects:

Participate in various finance projects including system implementation and upgrades, digital transformation initiatives, and other technology-enabled projects.
Support the design and implementation of controls within new business processes.
Assess risks and control requirements associated with system implementations and significant business changes.
Collaborate with project teams to ensure appropriate governance, security, and control considerations are incorporated into project plans.
Lead or participate in special projects, including process improvement initiatives, and other strategic initiatives.
Support management in evaluating the internal control impact of business transformation programs.

Executive Vice President of Project Management

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Vice President (EVP) of Project Management is responsible for providing comprehensive leadership and oversight of the company’s project management framework, project portfolio, and the execution of major projects. The EVP defines enterprise-level project management strategy, ensuring that all projects are implemented successfully in alignment with established strategic goals, budgetary plans, timelines, and quality standards. This role holds full accountability for project planning, execution, resource allocation, budget control, risk management, team leadership, and performance monitoring, with the objective of driving the standardization, formalization, and efficiency of the company’s project management system.

The EVP of Project Management is tasked with translating the company’s strategic objectives into actionable project plans, overseeing cross-departmental and cross-business-unit collaboration, and ensuring that major initiatives are delivered on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards. Working closely with the CEO, COO, CFO, heads of business units, and senior project management teams, the EVP provides strategic project management support for major investments, business transformation initiatives, and long-term development strategies, while continuously enhancing the organization’s overall project delivery capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

I. Project Management Strategy and Executive Leadership

Develop and implement an enterprise-wide project management strategy, ensuring that project management objectives are aligned with the company’s corporate strategy, operational plans, and long-term business goals. Provide comprehensive leadership to the project management department and relevant management teams, establishing unified standards, workflows, and execution mechanisms. Determine the direction, management priorities, and resource allocation plans for key projects based on the company’s business development needs. Monitor the execution of the project management strategy and provide regular reports to the CEO and senior leadership team regarding overall project progress, critical issues, and the outcomes of strategic implementation.

II. Project Portfolio Management and Prioritization

Assume full responsibility for the management and oversight of the company’s project portfolio. Evaluate the strategic value, commercial viability, resource requirements, and expected returns of individual projects to ensure that investments remain aligned with the company’s overall business objectives. Establish mechanisms for project initiation, approval, prioritization, and periodic review, while optimizing the allocation of resources and the sequence of execution across various projects. Oversee interdependencies, resource conflicts, and schedule coordination among multiple projects, adjusting the portfolio management plan as necessary. Collaborate with finance and business units to ensure that key projects receive the appropriate funding, personnel, and technical support. III. Project Planning and Execution Oversight

Lead the overall planning and execution management of major projects, ensuring that project scope, objectives, timelines, budgets, deliverables, and the division of responsibilities are clearly defined. Oversee project managers and their teams to ensure work progresses according to approved project plans, while conducting regular reviews of project milestones, task completion, and the quality of deliverables. For complex, cross-departmental, or high-priority projects, participate directly in key decision-making and execution oversight, addressing major issues that arise during implementation in a timely manner. Ensure that every phase of the project—from initiation, planning, and execution to monitoring and final delivery—complies with the company’s management requirements.

IV. Budget Management and Resource Allocation

Manage budget planning, cost oversight, and resource allocation at the project management level, collaborating with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and the finance department to establish project budgets, funding requirements, and cost-control plans. Monitor variances between actual expenditures and approved budgets, analyze the causes of any cost overruns, and develop appropriate corrective measures. Coordinate human resources, technical equipment, external vendors, and other necessary resources to ensure project teams possess the capabilities and conditions required to complete their tasks. Promote resource sharing and cross-project optimization to enhance resource utilization, reduce execution costs, and ensure that project investments yield the expected business value.

V. Project Performance and Schedule Management

Establish a unified corporate project performance management system and define key performance indicators (KPIs)—such as project completion rates, milestone achievement rates, budget and schedule variances, delivery quality, and project returns. Organize regular project review meetings to assess execution progress, cost status, and actual outcomes. Ensure that project managers submit timely progress reports, risk assessments, and performance analyses, enabling management to maintain an accurate understanding of project status. For projects experiencing delays, budget overruns, or quality issues, coordinate with relevant teams to develop recovery plans and improvement strategies, ensuring that projects are brought back on track.

VI. Cross-Departmental Coordination and Stakeholder Management

Foster effective collaboration between project management teams and various business functions—including operations, finance, engineering, technology, procurement, sales, marketing, and human resources—to ensure alignment on project objectives, resource allocation, and delivery requirements. Resolve conflicts regarding responsibilities, communication barriers, resource contention, or execution challenges that may arise in cross-departmental projects. Responsible for high-level communication with clients, suppliers, partners, and other key stakeholders to ensure that project requirements are accurately understood and critical matters are addressed in a timely manner. In the event of major project disputes or issues impacting overall delivery, organize relevant management personnel to develop and implement solutions.

VII. Project Risk, Quality, and Compliance Management

Establish an enterprise-level project risk management framework, overseeing project teams as they identify, assess, and manage potential risks related to schedules, budgets, technology, contracts, supply chains, and operations. Develop mechanisms for project risk reporting, issue escalation, and contingency response to ensure that significant risks are escalated promptly and resolved effectively. Collaborate with legal, compliance, quality management, and internal audit departments to ensure project execution adheres to applicable laws, regulations, contractual requirements, industry standards, and internal company policies. Supervise project quality control and delivery acceptance processes, drive the implementation of corrective and preventive actions, and mitigate the risks of project failure or operational losses.

VIII. Project Management System Optimization and Team Development

Continuously refine the company’s project management policies, standardized processes, and management tools, while advancing the development and operational capabilities of the Project Management Office (PMO). Introduce appropriate project management methodologies, digital management platforms, and data analytics technologies to enhance efficiency in project planning, schedule tracking, resource management, and performance reporting. Lead the development of project management talent, establishing performance evaluation, professional training, and succession planning mechanisms for project managers. Consolidate experience and best practices from major projects to foster knowledge sharing and continuous process improvement, thereby elevating the company’s professional standards in project management and its overall delivery capacity.

Work Experience

Typically requires 18+ years of experience in project management, project execution, engineering management, or corporate operations.

At least 8 years of senior management experience, with a proven track record of leading large-scale project management departments, Project Management Offices (PMOs), or multiple project teams.

Extensive experience in managing large project portfolios, complex cross-departmental projects, and enterprise-level strategic initiatives.

Practical management experience in areas such as strategic project planning, budget management, resource allocation, risk control, and project performance monitoring.

Preference will be given to candidates who have held positions such as Vice President of Project Management, Director of Project Management, Head of a Project Management Office (PMO), Head of Project Execution, or other senior leadership roles. Experienced in communicating and collaborating with CEOs, COOs, CFOs, and members of the Board of Directors.

Preference will be given to candidates with experience in managing cross-regional or international projects, or large-scale corporate transformation initiatives.

We are looking for a Director, Portfolio Management & Governance within the Technology Project Management Office.

The Director, Portfolio Management & Governance reports to the AVP, Program Management & Governance and is accountable for the integrated planning, governance, and delivery oversight of technology investments within the Canada Operations & Business Enablement portfolio. The Director works closely with senior business and technology leaders to establish priorities, evaluate investment trade-offs, manage portfolio-level risks and dependencies, and ensure initiatives deliver measurable business value within approved financial and capacity constraints. The role leads a team of Program Managers and Project Managers and serves as a trusted advisor and escalation point for portfolio delivery.

Planning:

Lead the development of the annual portfolio delivery plan and budget within Technology, and work with business partners to refresh a multi‑year delivery roadmap that aligns with strategic priorities.
Collaborate with Technology and Business Portfolio Leaders to assess and socialize priorities, ensuring visibility into impacts across systems, processes, and other portfolios.

Apply the most appropriate delivery methodologies—Waterfall, Agile (Scrum/Kanban), Hybrid, etc.—to achieve optimal business outcomes, ensuring adherence to enterprise standards and methodologies.

A university or college degree in a relevant field.

Proven ability to build strong, collaborative relationships with colleagues and external stakeholders, influencing outcomes with confidence and credibility.
Proven executive-level communication skills, with the ability to translate complex portfolio, delivery, financial, and risk information into clear, concise, decision-oriented messages for senior leaders. Demonstrated portfolio management experience, including investment planning, prioritization, financial forecasting, capacity planning, dependency management, and the evaluation of competing initiatives against business value and strategic outcomes.
Proven ability to apply sound judgment and constructive challenge within governance forums, including testing assumptions, identifying gaps, escalating concerns, and helping senior leaders make informed investment and delivery decisions.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing delivery professionals, including setting clear accountabilities, coaching performance, building succession capability, and creating an environment of transparency, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Ability to work across organizational boundaries and influence business and technology leaders with competing priorities, building alignment around enterprise outcomes rather than optimizing for a single project, function, or portfolio.
A strategic mindset with the ability to evaluate programs through the lens of business value and enterprise outcomes.
Strong comfort with ambiguity and change, with the ability to navigate uncertainty by seeking clarity from diverse stakeholders and available information.
Exceptional multi‑tasking and prioritization skills, thriving in a fast‑paced and demanding environment.
A passion for building, developing, and empowering high‑performing teams; a leader who models continuous learning, innovation, and an entrepreneurial mindset.

jobs.description:
About Vantage Group

Vantage Group is a global leader in airport and transportation investment, development, management, and advisor services. Since 1994, Vantage's corporate and network-wide team has managed an award-winning portfolio, building strong partnerships that integrate global expertise and local know-how to solve complex transportation challenges at every network location. Over three decades, Vantage has built a track record of creating customized solutions to transform airports and transportation centers that benefit the passengers, stakeholders, and communities they serve. Vantage is a wholly owned strategic platform of Investcorp Corsair Infrastructure Partners for capital deployment in the airport and transportation sectors. Visit vantagegroup.com to learn more.
Vantage Airport Group has operated the Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International Airport since 1997. Located in Moncton, New Brunswick, one of Atlantic Canada’s fastest-growing urban centres, the airport welcomed over 656,000 passengers in 2025 and serves as a key gateway for passenger and cargo traffic in the Maritime region. More information: www.cyqm.ca

The Role

The Greater Moncton International Airport Authority (GMIAA) is seeking a strategic and collaborative Director, Finance & Administration to serve as the organization’s senior financial leader and trusted advisor to the President & CEO, Board of Directors, and Audit Committee. This role is responsible for driving financial strategy, business planning, budgeting, risk management, and financial performance while ensuring strong governance and accountability across the organization.

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Director oversees all finance and administrative functions, including corporate finance, audits, insurance, pension and benefits programs, and corporate governance. The role also provides leadership and direction for the Human Resources function, supporting the development of a high-performing and engaged workforce. Working closely with internal teams, airline partners, vendors, and stakeholders, the successful candidate will help shape the airport’s long-term strategy and contribute to the continued growth and success of one of Atlantic Canada’s most important transportation hubs.

Key Responsibilities

Achievement of Financial Goals

As a member of the senior leadership team, partners with the CEO to translate the airport's strategic vision into long-term plans, annual business objectives, and measurable financial outcomes; leads initiatives that support sustainable growth and long-term financial viability.
Leads the annual business planning, budgeting, and forecasting processes, working collaboratively with all departments to develop financial plans that support organizational priorities.
Provides strategic financial analysis, insights, and recommendations to support operational, commercial, and capital investment decisions across the organization.
Leads the financial evaluation, negotiation, and ongoing performance monitoring of commercial agreements with airlines, concessionaires, tenants, and vendors.
Develops business cases and financial models for new projects, investments, and growth initiatives, ensuring informed decision-making and effective resource allocation.
Oversees capital planning and budgeting, including the development and maintenance of the airport's long-term capital plan.

Management & Performance Reporting

Serves as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors and Audit Committee, preparing and presenting financial reports, forecasts, business analyses, and recommendations.
Leads the development and continuous improvement of organizational performance measurement and reporting frameworks, ensuring key metrics effectively support accountability and strategic decision-making.
Ensures all organizational, financial, and regulatory reporting obligations are completed accurately and on time.

Finance & Administration Function

Provides overall leadership and accountability for the Finance & Administration function.
Oversees financial reporting, accounting operations, internal controls, treasury management, payroll oversight, tax compliance, and cash flow management.
Leads all external financial audits and serves as the primary liaison with auditors, financial institutions, and lending partners.
Manages the organization's insurance portfolio and enterprise risk management program, identifying and mitigating risks to support operational and financial objectives.
Serves as the organization's subject matter expert on airport fees and charges, Airport Improvement Fees (AIF), lease structures, and commercial pricing.
Ensures compliance with the Federal Ground Lease and related reporting, procurement, insurance, and public accountability requirements.

Leadership & Team Development

Leads the Finance & Administration team in a collaborative, high-performance environment, setting clear expectations and supporting employee growth, development, and succession planning.
Provides strategic leadership and oversight for the Human Resources function through the HR Manager, including workforce planning, employee relations, labour relations, and organizational effectiveness.
Oversees the Corporate Board Secretary function, ensuring effective governance processes, accurate board records, and administrative support for the Board of Directors.

Qualifications & Experience

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Commerce, or a related field.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation required.
Additional education or professional development in leadership, governance, risk management, or human resources would be considered an asset.

Experience

Minimum of 8 years of progressive leadership experience in finance and accounting, including at least 5 years in a senior management role.
Experience serving as a key member of a senior leadership team, contributing to organizational strategy, business planning, and decision-making.
Demonstrated success leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audits, treasury management, and risk management functions.
Experience presenting financial results, strategic recommendations, and business cases to Boards of Directors, Audit Committees, or similar governance bodies.
Experience evaluating, negotiating, and managing commercial agreements and business relationships with customers, vendors, tenants and airlines.
Experience providing leadership and oversight to human resources functions, including workforce planning and organizational development; direct HR leadership experience and labour relations is considered an asset.
Experience in the airport, aviation, transportation, infrastructure, or other capital-intensive industries would be considered an asset.
Bilingualism in English and French would be considered an asset.

Skills and Capabilities

Strategic and commercially minded leader with strong financial and business acumen.
Strong leadership, coaching, and team-building skills, with a track record of driving performance, accountability, and engagement.
Ability to lead organizational change and influence stakeholders at all levels, including executives, Board members, business partners, and external stakeholders.
Collaborative and approachable leadership style with a hands-on, solution-oriented approach.
Excellent verbal, written, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
High degree of integrity, professionalism, accountability, and sound judgment.

The expected annual compensation for this position includes a base salary of $130,000 to $155,000, plus eligibility to participate in the Company's annual incentive program. Beyond competitive compensation, we offer career progression opportunities, access to a global team of talented professionals, and boundless opportunities to make your mark within our organization. At a glance

Location: Montréal, QC. Hybrid, with about half your time on-site.
Employment: Full-time, permanent.
Reporting to: CFO.

About Nomic

Nomic was founded to make biology easier to measure—and to enable scientists to extend lives by making proteomics accessible, scalable, and routine. Our story began at McGill University, where our co-founders and early team developed breakthrough technology that would change the way proteins are measured.

Today, Nomic is powered by our proprietary nELISA® platform—an end-to-end technology that delivers high-throughput, quantitative, and affordable protein data at unprecedented scale. With the launch of Omni 1000, we are making the $50 proteome a reality, breaking down barriers that have limited the field for decades. For the first time, large-scale, quantitative proteomics is accessible to any scientist, supporting everything from drug discovery and translational research to AI-enabled therapeutic development.

Since our launch, we’ve partnered with leaders in pharma, biotech, and academia—including GlaxoSmithKline and the Broad Institute—and have profiled more than 500,000 samples across diverse applications. Our growth is fueled by over $60 million in investment from top-tier backers, including our recent $42 million Series B.

We’re building a team of world-changers—scientists, engineers, and problem-solvers who believe that accessible proteomics can help shape the future of medicine. If you want your work to have real impact, we’d love to meet you.

Learn more in our Series B announcement.

The role

As Director, Supply Chain, you will oversee end-to-end supply chain operations, including procurement, logistics, and inventory management. You will drive the development and execution of strategies to optimize performance, reduce costs, and improve reliability across systems and workflows. This role involves close collaboration with cross-functional teams to align production schedules, streamline material flow, and mitigate supply risks. You will also lead data-driven forecasting, manage supplier relationships, and establish clear metrics to monitor and continuously improve supply chain effectiveness. This role is ideal for someone with a strong track record in a high-growth environment, particularly in life sciences, and experience operating at the intersection of manufacturing and services.

What You’ll Do

Procurement

Own our material and product costs within our standard cost model, analyzing cost structure and inventory variances and leading improvements in cost efficiency.
Design and maintain procurement workflows that are scalable, automated and audit-ready, including for materials used in quality-controlled processes.
Develop sourcing strategies and manage supplier relationships, from negotiation to ongoing performance oversight.
Work with Sales, Manufacturing and Service Lab leaders to forecast material needs, using data-driven models and increasingly automated tools.

Sales and operations planning

Lead materials and supply planning with operational leaders, aligning production plans, raw material supply, inventory and supplier capacity with the sales forecast.
Build and maintain operational and capacity models that support resource planning and budgeting.
Own our ERP as its subject matter expert: data integrity, accuracy and how well it serves the business.

Inventory

Own our inventory systems and processes, with tight integration between the ERP and Nomic’s internally developed LIMS, the central hub for our operational data.
With your peers, set inventory carrying strategies that balance operational performance and financial stewardship.
Oversee receiving: intake, verification and system entry of inbound materials.
Keep physical inventory accurate across all storage sites, including temperature-controlled storage, and own material movement, reconciliation and audit readiness.
Track raw materials, work in progress and finished goods end to end, including lot traceability and shelf life.

Logistics

Build and run outbound logistics for our kit business: order fulfillment, packaging, shipping, temperature-controlled distribution, delivery tracking and returns.

What You’ll Bring

You’re naturally curious, quick to learn and energized by solving problems with people across disciplines. You think end to end, from planning and procurement to inventory and logistics, and you want to design systems that work well and scale from day one. You bring an engineering mindset, you’re comfortable with technology, and you care about making things run smoothly, reliably and transparently. You approach operations practically and iteratively, always looking for the next improvement.

You’ve seen what good looks like in a fast-growing manufacturing organization like ours. You know when to move fast, when to push back and when to step in and fix something yourself. You adapt how you work with others, handle change and ambiguity well, and colleagues trust you to bring structure without rigidity. You’re excited to be one of the first leaders of this function, knowing your work will help scientists better measure and understand biology.

Relevant experience. 7+ years in supply chain, operations or manufacturing roles supporting manufacturing. Life-science tools experience is strongly preferred; we also welcome candidates from other industries with strong technical adaptability.
Leadership and building experience. Experience leading and developing people. Building scalable processes in a high-growth company or having led a supply chain function is a plus.
Procurement and cost expertise. Experience owning strategic sourcing and supplier negotiations, and working with standard costing and variance analysis. Experience developing procurement practices in a quality-controlled environment is a plus.
Planning and inventory experience. Experience connecting sales forecasts to production and materials planning, with ownership of manufacturing inventory control. Experience shipping temperature-controlled goods is a plus.
ERP expertise. Subject matter expertise in an ERP system; NetSuite is highly desirable.
Cross-functional communication. You work effectively with scientific, operational and commercial teams and can turn complex requirements into practical processes.
Education. An advanced degree (for example an MSc) in engineering, the life sciences or a related technical field is a plus.
Location. You can work on-site in Montréal about half the time. Working proficiency in French and English is an asset.

Why join us

Real ownership. You’ll set the direction for Supply Chain and shape the processes, systems and workflows that support Nomic’s growth.
Work that matters. Our platform helps pharma, biotech and academic scientists understand disease and develop new medicines. A reliable supply chain is what keeps it running.

Nomic a été fondée pour faciliter la mesure biologique et permettre aux scientifiques de prolonger la vie en rendant la protéomique accessible, évolutive et courante. Notre histoire a commencé à l'Université McGill, où nos cofondateurs et notre équipe initiale ont mis au point une technologie révolutionnaire qui allait changer la façon dont les protéines sont mesurées.

Aujourd'hui, Nomic s'appuie sur notre plateforme exclusive nELISA®, une technologie de bout en bout qui fournit des données protéiques à haut débit, quantitatives et abordables à une échelle sans précédent. Avec le lancement d'Omni 1000, nous faisons du protéome à 50 dollars une réalité, brisant ainsi les barrières qui ont limité ce domaine pendant des décennies. Pour la première fois, la protéomique quantitative à grande échelle est accessible à tous les scientifiques, soutenant tout, de la découverte de médicaments et la recherche translationnelle au développement thérapeutique basé sur l'IA.

Depuis notre lancement, nous avons établi des partenariats avec des leaders du secteur pharmaceutique, des entreprises de biotechnologie et du secteur académique, notamment GlaxoSmithKline et le Broad Institute, et avons profilé plus de 500 000 échantillons dans diverses applications. .

Votre rôle

Vous dirigerez également les prévisions fondées sur les données, gérerez les relations avec les fournisseurs et établirez des indicateurs clairs pour suivre et améliorer continuellement l'efficacité de la chaîne d'approvisionnement. Ce poste conviendra parfaitement à une personne qui a fait ses preuves dans un environnement en forte croissance, en particulier dans les sciences de la vie, et qui a l'habitude d'évoluer à la jonction de la fabrication et des services.

Vos responsabilités

Assumer la responsabilité des coûts de nos matériaux et de nos produits dans le cadre de notre modèle de coût standard, en analysant la structure des coûts et les écarts d'inventaire et en dirigeant les initiatives d'amélioration de l'efficacité des coûts.

Collaborer avec les responsables des ventes, de la fabrication et du laboratoire de services afin de prévoir les besoins en matériaux, à l'aide de modèles fondés sur les données et d'outils de plus en plus automatisés.

Assumer la responsabilité de notre ERP à titre d'expert ou d'experte en la matière : intégrité et exactitude des données, et capacité du système à bien servir l'entreprise.

new_jobs.description:
Executive Vice President of Project Management

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Vice President (EVP) of Project Management is responsible for providing comprehensive leadership and oversight of the company’s project management framework, project portfolio, and the execution of major projects. The EVP defines enterprise-level project management strategy, ensuring that all projects are implemented successfully in alignment with established strategic goals, budgetary plans, timelines, and quality standards. This role holds full accountability for project planning, execution, resource allocation, budget control, risk management, team leadership, and performance monitoring, with the objective of driving the standardization, formalization, and efficiency of the company’s project management system.

The EVP of Project Management is tasked with translating the company’s strategic objectives into actionable project plans, overseeing cross-departmental and cross-business-unit collaboration, and ensuring that major initiatives are delivered on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards. Working closely with the CEO, COO, CFO, heads of business units, and senior project management teams, the EVP provides strategic project management support for major investments, business transformation initiatives, and long-term development strategies, while continuously enhancing the organization’s overall project delivery capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

I. Project Management Strategy and Executive Leadership

Develop and implement an enterprise-wide project management strategy, ensuring that project management objectives are aligned with the company’s corporate strategy, operational plans, and long-term business goals. Provide comprehensive leadership to the project management department and relevant management teams, establishing unified standards, workflows, and execution mechanisms. Determine the direction, management priorities, and resource allocation plans for key projects based on the company’s business development needs. Monitor the execution of the project management strategy and provide regular reports to the CEO and senior leadership team regarding overall project progress, critical issues, and the outcomes of strategic implementation.

Assume full responsibility for the management and oversight of the company’s project portfolio. Evaluate the strategic value, commercial viability, resource requirements, and expected returns of individual projects to ensure that investments remain aligned with the company’s overall business objectives. Establish mechanisms for project initiation, approval, prioritization, and periodic review, while optimizing the allocation of resources and the sequence of execution across various projects. Oversee interdependencies, resource conflicts, and schedule coordination among multiple projects, adjusting the portfolio management plan as necessary. Collaborate with finance and business units to ensure that key projects receive the appropriate funding, personnel, and technical support. III. Project Planning and Execution Oversight

Lead the overall planning and execution management of major projects, ensuring that project scope, objectives, timelines, budgets, deliverables, and the division of responsibilities are clearly defined. Oversee project managers and their teams to ensure work progresses according to approved project plans, while conducting regular reviews of project milestones, task completion, and the quality of deliverables. Partners with business continuity, disaster recovery and Technology teams to validate application recovery readiness, test critical dependencies and address resilience gaps.

Develops and maintains an enterprise-wide rolling multi-year application service and lifecycle roadmap aligned with business priorities, enterprise architecture and technology plans, balancing currency, resilience, supportability and cost.
Provides recommendations on application consolidation, retirement and standardization to reduce duplication, technical debt and operational complexity, with investment and architecture decisions made through established governance.
Leads vendor upgrades and patches through impact assessment, regression testing, cutover and stabilization, maintaining visibility into version currency, end-of-support exposure and remediation plans.
Delivers configuration changes and small enhancements on non-material initiatives, coordinating dependencies, release readiness and stakeholder communication to minimize member and employee disruption.

Introduces approved AI-enabled and automated practices for activities such as ticket triage, knowledge management, release analysis and regression testing, with human accountability and appropriate oversight.
Partners with business owners, Enterprise Transformation & Integration, and Technology teams to translate process improvements into supportable application changes, while preserving clear business, delivery and operational accountabilities.
Measures whether improvements reduce manual effort, recurring demand and service delays, and redirects released capacity toward higher-value work and priority commitments.

Partners with business and product teams to understand how application services enable everyday banking, digital engagement and advice-led relationships, translating those needs into clear operational priorities.
Collaborates with Architecture, Information Security, Infrastructure and Operations, Engineering, and Data teams to manage application dependencies and support consistent, reliable experiences across channels.

Responsible for application cost, usage and service insights to support budget planning, procurement decisions and vendor assessments.
Maintains visibility into application risks, control gaps and remediation commitments, providing decision-ready reporting on service health, lifecycle exposure, vendor performance, capacity and improvement outcomes.
Owns remediation commitments for application risks and controls gaps for their portfolio.

10+ years of progressive experience in application support, application management or IT service delivery, including senior people leadership experience.
Deep experience supporting business-critical applications in financial services, ideally including core banking, lending and digital banking platforms.
Strong grounding in service management practices, including incident, problem, change and release management; ITIL certification or equivalent experience is an asset.
Proven experience managing application vendors, service-level performance, escalations and upgrade coordination.
Demonstrated success planning and delivering application upgrades with disciplined regression testing and minimal member impact.
Experience with AI-enabled or agentic applications in production, or a strong interest in building this capability, including monitoring, evaluation and responsible change control.
Understanding of operational resilience, risk and control expectations within a regulated financial institution.
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across business and technical partners.
Working knowledge of modern service management and monitoring tools, such as ITSM platforms, application monitoring and observability tools, Azure DevOps or Jira.
An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Total Rewards:

Our total rewards approach reflects Beem's values — celebrating success, investing in your growth, and supporting you at work and in life.

Health & Wellness: Extended health coverage (including mental health support), dental care, and disability coverage

Nomic was founded to make biology easier to measure—and to enable scientists to extend lives by making proteomics accessible, scalable, and routine. Today, Nomic is powered by our proprietary nELISA® platform—an end-to-end technology that delivers high-throughput, quantitative, and affordable protein data at unprecedented scale. With the launch of Omni 1000, we are making the $50 proteome a reality, breaking down barriers that have limited the field for decades. Since our launch, we’ve partnered with leaders in pharma, biotech, and academia—including GlaxoSmithKline and the Broad Institute—and have profiled more than 500,000 samples across diverse applications. Our growth is fueled by over $60 million in investment from top-tier backers, including our recent $42 million Series B.

We’re building a team of world-changers—scientists, engineers, and problem-solvers who believe that accessible proteomics can help shape the future of medicine. If you want your work to have real impact, we’d love to meet you.

You’re excited to be one of the first leaders of this function, knowing your work will help scientists better measure and understand biology.

Real ownership. You’ll set the direction for Supply Chain and shape the processes, systems and workflows that support Nomic’s growth.
Work that matters. Our platform helps pharma, biotech and academic scientists understand disease and develop new medicines. A reliable supply chain is what keeps it running.

À propos de Nomic

Nomic a été fondée pour faciliter la mesure biologique et permettre aux scientifiques de prolonger la vie en rendant la protéomique accessible, évolutive et courante. Notre histoire a commencé à l'Université McGill, où nos cofondateurs et notre équipe initiale ont mis au point une technologie révolutionnaire qui allait changer la façon dont les protéines sont mesurées.

Aujourd'hui, Nomic s'appuie sur notre plateforme exclusive nELISA®, une technologie de bout en bout qui fournit des données protéiques à haut débit, quantitatives et abordables à une échelle sans précédent. Avec le lancement d'Omni 1000, nous faisons du protéome à 50 dollars une réalité, brisant ainsi les barrières qui ont limité ce domaine pendant des décennies. Pour la première fois, la protéomique quantitative à grande échelle est accessible à tous les scientifiques, soutenant tout, de la découverte de médicaments et la recherche translationnelle au développement thérapeutique basé sur l'IA.

Depuis notre lancement, nous avons établi des partenariats avec des leaders du secteur pharmaceutique, des entreprises de biotechnologie et du secteur académique, notamment GlaxoSmithKline et le Broad Institute, et avons profilé plus de 500 000 échantillons dans diverses applications. Notre croissance est alimentée par plus de 60 millions de dollars d'investissements provenant de bailleurs de fonds de premier plan, dont notre récente série B de 42 millions de dollars.

Nous constituons une équipe de personnes qui changent le monde : des scientifiques, des ingénieurs et des solutionneurs qui croient que la protéomique accessible peut contribuer à façonner l'avenir de la médecine. Si vous souhaitez que votre travail ait un impact réel, nous serions ravis de vous rencontrer.

Pour en savoir plus, consultez notre annonce de financement de série B
.

Votre rôle

À titre de directeur ou directrice de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, vous superviserez l'ensemble des activités de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, y compris l'approvisionnement, la logistique et la gestion des stocks. Vous piloterez l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de stratégies visant à optimiser le rendement, à réduire les coûts et à améliorer la fiabilité des systèmes et des processus. Ce rôle exige une collaboration étroite avec des équipes interfonctionnelles afin d'harmoniser les calendriers de production, de simplifier la circulation des matériaux et d'atténuer les risques d'approvisionnement. Vous dirigerez également les prévisions fondées sur les données, gérerez les relations avec les fournisseurs et établirez des indicateurs clairs pour suivre et améliorer continuellement l'efficacité de la chaîne d'approvisionnement. Ce poste conviendra parfaitement à une personne qui a fait ses preuves dans un environnement en forte croissance, en particulier dans les sciences de la vie, et qui a l'habitude d'évoluer à la jonction de la fabrication et des services.

Assumer la responsabilité des coûts de nos matériaux et de nos produits dans le cadre de notre modèle de coût standard, en analysant la structure des coûts et les écarts d'inventaire et en dirigeant les initiatives d'amélioration de l'efficacité des coûts.

Collaborer avec les responsables des ventes, de la fabrication et du laboratoire de services afin de prévoir les besoins en matériaux, à l'aide de modèles fondés sur les données et d'outils de plus en plus automatisés.

new_jobs.description:
You’ve built dashboards. Tracked milestones. Chased vendors. Flagged risks. But your reports hit a ceiling. You weren’t the one making the calls.

2 Hour Learning is building an AI-powered education model designed to help students achieve a full day of academic progress in just two hours. Making that model work at scale requires dozens of initiatives, technology partners, contracts, and investment decisions to move in sync. Your job is to make the execution layer trustworthy enough for executives to act on it.

You will own the operating outputs behind those decisions: portfolio dashboards that expose slippage before it becomes a surprise, vendor scorecards tied to real contractual commitments, competitive bid packages that make trade-offs clear, and contract controls that prevent unsupported spend. AI will be part of your daily workflow, helping you standardize updates, detect anomalies, compare bids, analyze vendor performance, and validate invoices.

This is not a PMO role built around meetings, process compliance, or polished status decks. It is for an operator who wants their work to have consequences. When a vendor underperforms, your evidence should make that obvious. When spend drifts from the contract, your controls should catch it. When executives need to make a $5M decision, your outputs should give them the confidence to make it fast. If that sounds like the level of ownership you have been looking for, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Own portfolio-level dashboards across 10+ concurrent initiatives, using AI to standardize updates, detect slippage, expose blockers, and maintain a trusted executive view of delivery, budget, and risk
Run recurring vendor performance reviews and maintain rubric-based scorecards that combine delivery, quality, cost, contractual commitments, and qualitative performance signals
Lead competitive technology-vendor procurement, including structured bid packages, normalized comparisons, scoring rubrics, SOW development, and evidence-backed recommendations
Govern contracts and invoices by tracking fee caps, milestones, acceptance criteria, and amendments, then validating invoices against signed terms before spend is approved
Use AI daily to analyze portfolio data, detect anomalies, surface underperformance, draft decision-ready outputs, and reduce manual PMO administration

What You Won’t Be Doing

Producing status reports that executives read but never use to make decisions
Running a meeting-heavy PMO where coordination matters more than measurable execution
Treating vendor management as relationship maintenance while missed commitments go unchallenged
Passing contracts, SOWs, invoices, or procurement decisions to someone else because they look too commercial or technical
Using AI as an occasional productivity trick instead of a core part of how you operate

VP Portfolio Operations Key Responsibilities

As VP Portfolio Operations, you will produce reliable, AI-powered dashboards, scorecards, procurement packages, and contract controls that give executives the clarity and leverage to hold vendors accountable, control costs, and accelerate delivery across a $50M EdTech portfolio.

Basic Requirements

Personally owned execution across 10+ concurrent initiatives with at least $5M in portfolio budget responsibility, tracking spend and making evidence-backed recommendations on budget allocation, vendor selection, and initiative priorities. Final approval authority and P&L ownership are not required
Managed 5+ external technology vendors at the same time, such as SaaS providers, AI/ML platforms, marketing agencies, or engineering firms
Built and maintained portfolio-level dashboards covering metrics such as delivery health, budget burn versus forecast, milestone completion, and major risks or blockers
Can point to a case where C-suite leaders used your portfolio data to make a go/no-go decision on a vendor renewal, budget reallocation, or initiative deprioritization
Directly led competitive technology procurement, including structured bid evaluation, vendor scoring, negotiation, and recommendations for executive approval
Authored or co-authored SOWs with measurable deliverables, milestone payments, SLAs, acceptance criteria, or other performance-based terms
Negotiated commercial terms such as pricing, penalties, fee caps, or exit clauses and enforced those terms through invoice validation or corrective action
Strong written communication skills, with the ability to turn complex financial and operational data into concise recommendations executives can act on
Able to analyze financial and vendor-performance data quickly enough to recommend optimization, reallocation, or vendor elimination
Able to work US business hours

Nice-to-have Requirements

Experience using AI-enabled dashboards, anomaly detection, predictive alerts, or natural-language analysis in portfolio management
Experience in EdTech, technology, consulting, or another environment managing complex portfolios of external technology partners
Fluency with portfolio and delivery tools such as Linear, Jira, or similar systems

About 2 Hour Learning

Education is broken, but 2 Hour Learning is proving it doesn’t have to be. They’re tearing down the outdated one-size-fits-all model and replacing it with AI-driven personalized learning that helps kids master academics in just two hours a day.

With students consistently ranking in the top 1-2% nationally and the top 20% achieving an astonishing 6.5x growth, they’re proving that smarter learning is possible. At 2 Hour Learning, it’s talent and performance that matter.

They offer a dynamic, on-campus and remote-friendly environment where innovators, educators, and AI specialists can be a part of fixing a broken school system.

2 Hour Learning is reprogramming learning for the AI era.

Here’s How They’re Fixing It.
